key_insight: RESCUE treats model failures as sparse internal computation errors, then localizes and edits the responsible circuit to fix performance while largely preserving other abilities.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a targeted, low-drift debugging workflow for LLMs, suggesting safer and more efficient repair than broad fine-tuning when a specific task failure must be corrected.
method: Use mechanistic interpretability to identify error-associated sparse circuits.
Refine circuit masks with reinforcement learning over multiple masked-model rollouts to better capture generation-time failures.
Prune and fine-tune only the selected error circuit for surgical model repair.
evidence_signal: On math reasoning, a 1.40% density circuit improved accuracy from 6.0% to 75.5%, and on medical QA, a 1.44% circuit raised repair-set accuracy from 0% to 81%.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable error localization and careful mask optimization; if the identified circuit is incomplete or noisy, repair may not generalize beyond the evaluated task set.
paper_title: RESCUE: Repairing Language Model Errors to Sparse Circuits via Reinforcement Learning
